reason: Rank the 32-row classical panel first: it is a distinct change to the active n=512 path and tests a bounded working-set hypothesis, though its compute and pointer changes carry correctness risk. The fused decrement and branch is a small, low-risk change to the measured hot loop, but no evidence shows loop control limits performance. The Strassen zero-fill removal is a distinct, limited attempt to reduce overhead, yet the measured three-buffer Strassen wrapper lost all ten paired runs; that result does not isolate the cause. Explicit NEON packing may help only if the compiler does not already vectorize those loops. A single workspace allocation has uncertain benefit and may fail where separate allocations succeed. Tail splitting affects the general fallback rather than the fixed n=512 timing and adds edge-handling risk. The product-buffer proposal appears to repeat the existing reusable-product schedule, so it may not produce a distinct source change. Transpose fusion rereads A sixteen times and adds repeated transpose work; its expected costs make it the weakest proposal. All predicted effects remain unverified.
